svg.text: The same pipeline, eight eras: host software (gray), dedicated hardware (blue), programmable GPU (orange)

g.text: Era 1: vector display with a display processor
Sketchpad on the TX-2 (1963) drew from the main program; the IBM 2250 (1964) refreshed its own display list
era-specific units sit below the stage they serve
Era 2: host computer plus frame buffer
E&S frame buffer at NYIT, 1975: 512 by 512 by 8 bits, $80,000
era-specific units sit below the stage they serve
SGI IRIS (1983 on) with Clark’s Geometry Engine (1982)
era-specific units sit below the stage they serve
3dfx Voodoo Graphics card, 1996, $299: "only accelerates the inner rasterization loop"
era-specific units sit below the stage they serve
NVIDIA GeForce 256, 1999: "15 million sustained polygons per second"; card $349.99
era-specific units sit below the stage they serve
Era 6: programmable vertex and pixel stages
NVIDIA GeForce3 (2001), programmable vertex engine; ATI Radeon 9700 (2002), programmable pixels
era-specific units sit below the stage they serve
Era 7: unified shaders and GPU compute
NVIDIA GeForce 8800 GTX, 2006: 128 unified stream processors, $599; CUDA 2007
era-specific units sit below the stage they serve
Era 8: ray-tracing cores, tensor cores, mesh shaders
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 (Turing), 2018: RT cores, tensor cores, $699
era-specific units sit below the stage they serve
